summary: Problem 9 (combinatorial identities for lattice paths / hook coefficients) has a substantially complete proof draft (13,717 chars) that the rubric rates highly: correct answer, Logic 9/10, Completeness 8/10, Clarity 9/10. The core derivation — coefficient-extraction recurrence telescoping into a signed formula, then a Sagan–Swanson sign-reversing involution proving positivity — is sound and verified consistent on n=2. The main weakness is that one lemma (phiaction) cites Sagan–Swanson structural facts without re-deriving them, leaving a self-containment gap rather than a logical error.
problems: Lemma phiaction(i) relies on asserted Sagan–Swanson facts about type-III structure ('all blocks size 1', 'maxima increasing so inv=0') without re-derivation, so the proof is not fully self-contained.
Completeness scored 8/10: the involution's type-III handling and cancellation of type-I(c<b) ↔ type-II pairings is described but leans on external citations at the critical step.
The single open issue (Proof: Problem 9) remains open and the draft is on record but not yet verified, so positivity of the hook coefficients is not yet certified end-to-end.
highlights: Answer is correct (1/1) and produces a manifestly positive combinatorial formula for the hook coefficients.
Coefficient-extraction recurrence and its telescoping into the signed formula are correct and verified consistent for n=2.
Sign-reversing involution is carefully partitioned: exactly the type-I elements in the c=b summand survive, with type-I(c<b) ↔ type-II pairing shown to cancel fully.
High rubric marks across Logic (9/10) and Clarity (9/10) indicate a well-executed, readable derivation.

suggested_todos.title: Re-derive the Sagan–Swanson type-III structural facts ('all blocks size 1', 'maxima increasing ⇒ inv=0') inline within Lemma phiaction to make it self-contained
Add an explicit verification of the involution's well-definedness and full cancellation for the type-I(c<b) ↔ type-II pairing, ideally checked on n=3 as well as n=2
